questions.stem: In the evolution towards Augmented Analytics, who defined data elements in the first approach, the classic semantic layer?
questions.explanation: In the first approach, the Semantic Layer, IT defines data elements for business ease.

questions.stem: In the second approach preceding Augmented Analytics, who defines data elements?
options: Business folks themselves, based on their own understanding
questions.explanation: In the second era, business folks define data elements themselves based on their own understanding.

questions.stem: What is Augmented Analytics based on?
options: Manual definition of data elements by IT
Static requirements gathered once from the business
Automated Machine Learning that learns data elements as new datasets keep coming in
questions.explanation: Augmented Analytics is based on automated Machine Learning, which learns the data elements while new datasets keep coming in.

questions.stem: What is the major difference between the first two approaches and Augmented Analytics?
options: The first two were derived by humans, with the risk of human error and bias; Augmented Analytics is automated
The first two used unstructured data; Augmented Analytics uses structured data
Augmented Analytics requires more manual effort
The first two were fully automated; Augmented Analytics is manual
questions.explanation: The first two approaches were derived by humans, either IT or business, so there is always a factor of human error and possible bias based on the knowledge they possess; Augmented Analytics is based on automated Machine Learning.

questions.stem: Why was the first approach, where IT implemented business requirements, described as static?
options: Because it used only static reports
Because business users could change it at will
Because it ran on machine learning
Because it was implemented in a data lake
Because requirements always came from business and were implemented by IT, so any change had a round-robin effect
questions.explanation: The first approach was static: requirements always came from business and were implemented by IT folks, so any change had a round-robin effect.

questions.stem: How is the second approach, where business designs and implements data elements itself, characterised?
questions.explanation: The second approach was flexible, as businesses were designing and implementing themselves; the first was static and the third is very dynamic.

questions.stem: How is the third and latest approach, Augmented Analytics, characterised?
options: Very dynamic, with ML models learning, designing, updating, upgrading and implementing the semantic layer automatically
questions.explanation: The third approach is very dynamic, where ML models are learning, designing, updating, upgrading and implementing the semantic layer automatically.

questions.stem: In Augmented Analytics, ML models define data elements based on what kind of requirements?
questions.explanation: The latest approach is going towards Machine Learning models defining data elements based on open-ended requirements.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the three approaches to defining data elements described on the way to Augmented Analytics?
options: IT defines data elements for business ease
Business folks define data elements themselves
Machine learning models define data elements automatically
Regulators define data elements for all organisations
All three of the approaches named are correct
questions.explanation: The three approaches are IT-defined, business-defined and ML-defined; regulators defining data elements is not one of them.

questions.stem: Why may human-defined semantic layers, whether by IT or business, be biased?
options: Because humans can be biased based on the knowledge and information they possess about the business domain
Because humans always favour structured data
Because the business never shares requirements
questions.explanation: Humans can be biased based on the knowledge and information they possess about the business domain, which is a factor in the first two approaches but not in automated Augmented Analytics.
